brief.summary_1line: Death, sent by Brahma, tells Rama his divine mission is fulfilled and reminds him of his origin as Vishnu who incarnated to destroy Ravana.

image_candidates.scene_text: The ascetic revealing himself as Death stands before Rama in a guarded chamber while Lakshmana waits outside the closed door.
Death proclaims Rama as the cosmic Vishnu from whose navel a radiant lotus emerges bearing Brahma.

deep.rich_summary: Lakshmana is ordered to guard the door so that Rama may speak privately with a mysterious ascetic whose message must be heard by no one else. The visitor reveals his true identity: he is Death itself, once a son of the cosmic Grandsire (Brahma), sent to deliver a divine message. Brahma declares that Rama’s mission on earth is fulfilled. The speech recalls the primordial acts of the divine—creation from the lotus arising from Vishnu’s navel, the slaying of Madhu and Kaitabha, and the sustaining of the worlds. It also reminds Rama that he incarnated as a man to destroy Ravana when the demon threatened all beings. The moment reframes Rama not merely as a king but as Vishnu incarnate whose earthly role is nearing completion.

top_scenes.scene_text: In a sealed royal chamber, Rama sits facing a mysterious ascetic as Lakshmana stands guard outside the door under the threat of death for any interruption.
The ascetic reveals his true form as Death, delivering Brahma’s cosmic message to Rama in a dimly lit chamber.
A mythic vision of creation: a radiant lotus emerging from Vishnu’s navel while the bodies of Madhu and Kaitabha form the earth beneath towering mountains.
